classification.difficultyReason: With perpendicular radii and equal tangent lengths explicitly supplied, recognise the square at the right-angle corner and express the two legs using the hypotenuse's tangent segments.

content.prompt:
The hypotenuse of a right-angled triangle is $15\text{ cm}$. A circle of radius $2\text{ cm}$ is drawn inside the triangle so that it touches each of the three sides. What is the perimeter of the triangle?

Hint: A radius drawn to a point where a side touches the circle is perpendicular to that side. The two tangent segments from the same vertex to their points of contact have equal lengths.

answer.short:
$34\text{ cm}$

Equal tangent lengths give the sum of the legs as the hypotenuse plus twice the incircle radius.
answer.worked:
The radii to the points of contact are perpendicular to the sides. At the right-angle vertex, the two contact points and the circle's centre therefore form a square of side $2\text{ cm}$.

Let the tangent lengths from the other two vertices be $x\text{ cm}$ and $y\text{ cm}$. Tangents from the same vertex have equal lengths, so the hypotenuse is $x+y$ and the legs are $x+2$ and $y+2$.

$$\begin{align*}x+y&=15\\P&=(x+2)+(y+2)+(x+y)\\P&=2(x+y)+4\\P&=2\times15+4\\P&=34\text{ cm}\end{align*}$$
